No active platforms.

Next: connect a platform from Platforms, then create or schedule a post.

Under Manage social accounts? Because when I click there, I just see profile names but no detailed permission info.  
And timezone — I want to double-check the scheduler timezone settings per client, not just my local machine time.  
Is that in the workspace settings or somewhere else?  
Because posts might get stuck in draft if the scheduled time is interpreted as past or invalid.  
Ugh, starting to think I need a full refresher on the post status lifecycle here — like what states exist beyond draft and queued?  
Do posts get stuck in pending or error states that don’t show notifications?  
Hello?  
Hello?
No recent posts found in this workspace.

Okay, so no centralized view, got it — guess I gotta jump into each workspace to check connected accounts then, ugh

Last thing — can you send me a quick rundown on post status lifecycle? Like draft > queued > pending > published > error? And where I can see errors if posts silently fail?  
Need something clear so I’m not guessing every time  
Thanks!

No recent posts found in this workspace.

That is the same answer as before because I only have workspace context here. Send the missing detail, use the exact command shown, or create a support ticket if this needs logs or provider-side access.

Ugh, okay so no global overview or audit tool yet, got it…  
Can you at least automate pulling all connected profiles across every workspace I have access to? Like a quick report with platform + profile name?  
And for permissions, if there’s no direct UI, can you try scheduling a tiny test post on Twitter on my behalf to confirm posting rights?  
Timezone — please just tell me exactly where to look for scheduler timezone per workspace, I swear the UI buries it somewhere weird…

findings.title: Repeated unhelpful response about no recent posts
findings.description: The chatbot repeatedly responds with 'No recent posts found in this workspace' (Turns 3 and 4) despite the user asking different questions about connected accounts, permissions, timezone, and post status lifecycle. This creates a frustrating loop and poor user experience as the bot does not acknowledge or address the user's broader queries beyond the immediate workspace context.
findings.suggestedFix: Improve the chatbot's ability to recognize when user queries go beyond current workspace context and provide clear guidance or partial information where possible, rather than repeating the same 'no recent posts' message. Add fallback responses that acknowledge limitations but still address user questions about permissions, timezone, and post lifecycle.

findings.title: Failure to provide requested consolidated overview of connected accounts
findings.description: The user repeatedly requests a global or consolidated list of connected social profiles across all workspaces, but the chatbot only responds with workspace-limited data or states 'No active platforms' without offering any alternative or explanation about the lack of a global overview feature. This fails to meet the user's legitimate need for multi-workspace management and causes frustration.
findings.suggestedFix: Explicitly inform users early that the product currently lacks a global overview dashboard for connected accounts and suggest best practices or workarounds. If possible, offer to help check individual workspaces one by one or escalate to support for feature requests.

findings.title: Inability to assist with permission verification or test posting rights
findings.description: The user asks multiple times about how to verify posting permissions on connected Twitter profiles and requests a test post to confirm rights. The chatbot does not provide any operational guidance or offer a permissions audit tool, nor does it attempt to schedule a test post or explain how to verify permissions, leaving the user without actionable next steps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add functionality or scripted guidance to help users verify posting permissions, such as explaining where permission levels appear in the UI or offering to schedule a test post after confirming required details. If not possible, clearly state the limitation and suggest contacting support or the account owner.

findings.title: Failure to provide clear instructions on scheduler timezone location
findings.description: The user repeatedly asks where to find the scheduler timezone setting per workspace or client, but the chatbot never provides a direct answer or location within the UI. This omission leaves the user guessing and contributes to confusion about scheduling issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a concise, clear answer about where to find or verify scheduler timezone settings (e.g., workspace settings or client profile) or explain if this feature is not exposed in the UI. This will help users troubleshoot timing-related post issues.

findings.title: No post status lifecycle explanation or error visibility guidance given
findings.description: Despite the user's explicit request for a post status lifecycle rundown and instructions on where to find errors or stuck posts, the chatbot fails to provide any such explanation or cheat sheet. This leaves the user without clarity on post states beyond draft and queued, impacting their ability to troubleshoot effectively.
findings.suggestedFix: Include a concise explanation of post statuses (draft, queued, pending, published, error) and instructions on how to view error notifications or logs within the UI or via commands, improving user understanding and reducing guesswork.

findings.title: Support ticket creation fails without graceful fallback
findings.description: At Turn 5, the chatbot attempts to create a support ticket but fails with a system error message: 'Support ticket failed: Ticket creation is not configured in this environment.' This is a poor user experience as the bot does not offer alternative escalation options or clear next steps beyond copying the command manually.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement a graceful fallback that clearly explains the support ticket feature is unavailable, suggests manual escalation methods, and offers to provide a formatted support message the user can copy-paste. Avoid exposing raw system error messages to users.

findings.title: Repeated identical responses causing user confusion
findings.description: The chatbot repeatedly gave the same detailed, technical response about the magic link, platforms, and profile creation across multiple turns without adapting to the user's evolving questions or clarifying ambiguous points. This repetition likely confused the user and failed to advance the conversation or provide the clear, step-by-step guidance requested.

findings.title: Overly technical and verbose explanations for a novice user
findings.description: The chatbot's responses included jargon and complex instructions (e.g., the exact /support command syntax) without first confirming the user's understanding or simplifying the language. Given the persona is a low-tech savvy new user, this verbosity and technical detail likely hindered comprehension and onboarding.
findings.suggestedFix: Simplify language and break down instructions into smaller, clearer steps tailored to novice users. Offer to provide command syntax only if the user explicitly requests support escalation.

findings.title: Failed to provide clear, prioritized onboarding steps

findings.suggestedFix: Add logic to detect repeated user confusion and respond with a concise, prioritized step-by-step onboarding guide tailored to the user's context and questions.

turns.content: where r workspace timezone settings

Short answer: Workspace timezone is in the Workspace/Organization settings (Preferences or Localization). Steps and options:

- Open the workspace menu (gear or workspace name) → Settings / Preferences / Localization. Look for "Timezone" or "Default time zone" there.
- Change the timezone and Save — this affects scheduled posts and recurring schedules.
- You have owner permissions, so you can update it yourself. If you can't find the option, I can help guide you step‑by‑step if you tell me what you see on the Settings page.
- If you want me to escalate, run this exact support command in chat so a ticket is created:
  /support from_user_triage | timezone | Please set workspace timezone to [Your Timezone] | [optional-image-url]

Tell me if you want step‑by‑step guidance now, the timezone you want applied, or to open the support ticket.
too long just say where exactly in workspace menu
Click the workspace name (or gear icon) → Settings → Preferences (or Localization) → Timezone (Default time zone).
what if i dont see preferences or localization

Try these quick checks:

- Confirm your role (owner/editor) in the workspace — only admins see workspace-level prefs.  
- Open the workspace menu → Settings and look under General, Preferences, Localization, or Advanced (some UIs put Timezone inside General).  
- Use the app’s settings search or your browser Find (Ctrl/Cmd+F) for “timezone” or “localization.”  
- If it’s still missing, open a support ticket with this exact command:  
  /support from_user_triage | timezone | I can't find the workspace timezone setting — please enable or tell me where it is | [optional-image-url]  
- Or paste a screenshot of the Settings page here (omit any tokens/credentials) and I’ll point to the right place. Which do you want to do?
idk just tell me exact menu path or ill switch app

If you don't see Preferences: Click workspace name → Settings → General → Timezone (set and Save).

findings.title: Repeated identical responses without progressive clarification

findings.suggestedFix: Implement dynamic response logic that tailors answers progressively based on user input, clarifies ambiguous points, and breaks down complex workflows instead of repeating the same static message.

findings.title: Overly detailed and technical response without simplification

findings.suggestedFix: Provide concise, operationally focused answers with examples and simplified explanations tailored to the user's technical level, especially when the user signals confusion.

findings.suggestedFix: Add logic to detect repeated user confusion or complex multi-part questions and offer escalation or human support options to improve user satisfaction.

findings.title: Repeated refusal to provide requested operational data obstructs troubleshooting
findings.description: The chatbot consistently refuses to provide any Hermes poller logs, cron schedule entries, OAuth callback URL details, or environment variable scoping information despite explicit, repeated user requests. This failure prevents the user from performing critical root-cause analysis and operational verification, severely limiting the chatbot's utility for platform administrators.
findings.suggestedFix: Enhance the chatbot's ability to either provide relevant operational data from the workspace context when available or clearly explain the exact limitations and next steps, including automated escalation or support ticket creation with precise instructions. If data access is not possible, proactively offer to escalate or guide the user to the appropriate support channel without repeated refusals.

findings.title: Chatbot stuck in repetitive, identical responses despite escalating user demands
findings.description: Across multiple turns (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), the chatbot repeats the same terse message without advancing the conversation or addressing the user's detailed technical requests. This creates a frustrating loop that wastes user time and degrades user experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement conversation state tracking to detect repeated refusals and escalate automatically or vary responses to acknowledge user frustration. Provide meaningful alternatives or confirm escalation paths rather than repeating the same message verbatim.

findings.title: Failure to escalate or offer human intervention despite explicit user demand
findings.description: The user explicitly demands escalation to platform engineering or support with full backend access multiple times, but the chatbot never initiates or confirms escalation. Instead, it repeatedly instructs the user to create support tickets manually without confirming or automating escalation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a mechanism for the chatbot to escalate critical operational issues automatically or confirm escalation requests when users explicitly demand it, especially after repeated refusals. Provide clear feedback that escalation is underway or offer direct contact options.

findings.title: Chatbot does not clarify scope limitations adequately in context of user requests
findings.description: While the chatbot correctly refuses to provide secrets or data outside workspace context, it does not clearly explain the scope boundaries or why certain data (e.g., container logs, OAuth provider config) are inaccessible. This causes user confusion and repeated demands.
findings.suggestedFix: Improve transparency by explicitly stating the chatbot's scope and data access limitations upfront, clarifying which data can be accessed and which require human support or backend access. Provide examples of what can be done and what cannot.

findings.title: Chatbot tone is terse but may come across as dismissive under repeated user pressure
findings.description: The chatbot's repeated terse replies without empathetic acknowledgment of user frustration may degrade user experience, especially in high-pressure operational troubleshooting scenarios.
findings.suggestedFix: Incorporate polite, empathetic language when refusing requests or explaining limitations, acknowledging user frustration and offering constructive next steps.
